lines.japanese: いや、終わらないよ？
lines.english: No, it isn't over.

lines.japanese: 「おおっ！　さすがに盛りあがってるな」
lines.english: “Whoa! This place is hopping!”

lines.japanese: 「あぁ、どこまでもびっしり……」
lines.english: “Ugh. People packed in as far as I can see...”

lines.japanese: 鳥居をくぐるや、人ごみの苦手な山科京がうめくように呟いた。
lines.english: The moment we passed beneath the shrine gate, Kyou Yamashina, who hated crowds, gave a low groan.

lines.japanese: しかし果てまで並ぶ露店の列に迎えられて、俄然勢いづく者もいた。
lines.english: Others, however, were instantly reinvigorated by the endless rows of festival stalls that greeted us.

lines.japanese: 渡来明日香だ。
lines.english: Asuka Watarai was one of them.

lines.japanese: 「おおっ、金魚すくい。射的も型抜きもあるじゃん。いいねえ、童心に返れるねえ、ノスタルジックだねえ」
lines.english: “Ooh, goldfish scooping. They've got a shooting gallery and candy cutting too. Nice. Makes you feel like a kid again. So nostalgic.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　渡来ってこういうお祭りごと、盛りあがるタイプだったか？」
lines.english: “Was Watarai always the type to get excited over festivals like this?”

lines.japanese: 針生蔵人に訊ねてみると、彼はせわしなく四方八方を見渡しながらぼんやり答えた。
lines.english: I asked Kuroudo Hariu. He answered vaguely while busily looking in every direction.

lines.japanese: 「あァ、あいつ学園の体育祭だの文化祭だのには同調しないけど、キホンこういう童心に返れるってシチュエーションには弱いみたいだなァ。知らねえけど、幼少時代になんか執着でもあんじゃねえの」
lines.english: “Yeah. She won't play along at school sports festivals or cultural festivals, but she's basically a sucker for anything that lets her feel like a kid again. Don't ask me. Maybe she's hung up on her childhood or something.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、そうなのか。だが、いまなお少年時代の冒険心を失わない無邪気な俺としては気が合いそうだな」
lines.english: “Huh. Is that so? Then she should get along splendidly with an innocent soul like me, who retains the adventurous spirit of boyhood even now.”

lines.japanese: 思いかえせば二週間ほど前、みんなで初詣に行こうなどと言いだしたのは他でもない渡来明日香だった。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Asuka Watarai herself had proposed that we all go for the first shrine visit about two weeks earlier.

lines.japanese: 俺の中の五分の二は言うまでもなく騒ぎ好きだし、残り五分の三とてあまり表には出さないものの元来イベント事は好きな方なのだ。
lines.english: Two fifths of me were fond of noisy excitement, of course. The remaining three fifths did not show it as openly, but each was naturally rather fond of special occasions too.

lines.japanese: ゆえに深く考えず「うひょー、初詣だでー」程度の軽い気持ちで賛同したのだが。
lines.english: So I agreed without much thought, in the casual spirit of “Woo-hoo, first shrine visit!”

lines.japanese: 「うひょー、初詣だぜー！」
lines.english: “Woo-hoo, first shrine visit!”

lines.japanese: うぉんむ、うぉんむ。渡来明日香も盛りあがっておるな。
lines.english: Wom, wom. Asuka Watarai appears to be in high spirits as well.

lines.japanese: 「わっ、キメドラヘヴンのお面！　ねねね、欲しくない？　アレ欲しくないぱね島くん？　欲しいよね欲しいに違いないよね、ちょっと買ってくるよぱね村ぱね夫くん」
lines.english: “Whoa, an *Ultrameth Heaven* mask! Hey, hey, don't you want it? Don't you want that, Paneshima? You do, you definitely do. I'll go buy it for you, Paneo Panemura!”

lines.japanese: 「いや、待つんだ渡山渡子さん」
lines.english: “No, wait, Wataruko Watayama.”

lines.japanese: 「じょわっ！？」
lines.english: “Jwah?!”

lines.japanese: 俺は渡来明日香のクソ長い髪をむんずと掴んで引きとめた。
lines.english: I seized Asuka Watarai by her ridiculously long hair and held her back.

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿者、団体行動を乱すでない。バイトの受付時間に遅れるだろう」
lines.english: “Fool. Do not disrupt the group's formation. We will be late for the part-time-job check-in.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そっか。うちら遊びに来たわけじゃないんだもんね」
lines.english: “Oh, right. We didn't come here to have fun.”

lines.japanese: そう。
lines.english: Indeed.

lines.japanese: 俺と渡来明日香は、今夜この神社でなんと獅子舞のアルバイトをするのだ。
lines.english: Tonight, Asuka Watarai and I would be working at this shrine as the two performers inside a lion-dance costume.

lines.japanese: 発端は、二学期の終わりごろ教室で交わしていた雑談だ。
lines.english: It had begun with some casual conversation in the classroom near the end of the second term.

lines.japanese: よく覚えていないのだが、そのとき俺とやつは、獅子舞の中の人をやりたいなどと言っていたらしい。
lines.english: I did not remember it well, but apparently the two of us had said we wanted to be the people inside a lion costume.

lines.japanese: 厳密に言えば『爆笑！　ゆく年くる年バトル一番・獅子舞ＶＳなまはげ世紀の対決スペシャル』をやりたいなどとほざいていたらしい。
lines.english: More precisely, we had babbled something about staging *Laugh Riot! New Year's Eve Battle Number One: Lion Dance vs. Namahage, the Showdown of the Century Special*.

lines.japanese: もちろん俺たちにとってそんなものは、例によって考えなしに発言した恒例のハチャメチャトークに過ぎなかったので、ほとんど覚えてさえいなかったのだが──
lines.english: Naturally, it had been nothing more than our customary nonsense, spoken without a moment's thought, and neither of us even remembered most of it—

lines.japanese: ──どうも山科京の耳には、印象強く残っていたらしい。
lines.english: —but it had apparently left a powerful impression on Kyou Yamashina.

lines.japanese: 基本的には消極的で主張しないタチの彼女だが、何故だかときおり恐ろしくテンションの高い日がある。
lines.english: She was generally passive and reluctant to assert herself, but for some reason she occasionally had days of terrifyingly high energy.

lines.japanese: そんな状態のとき、ついつい美空神社に突撃電話をして、なかば無理矢理シロート獅子舞の約束を取りつけてしまったというのだ。
lines.english: While in such a state, she had impulsively called Misora Shrine and all but forced them to promise that two amateurs could perform the lion dance.

lines.japanese: 「まったく、困ったもんだ……」
lines.english: “Honestly. What a mess...”

lines.japanese: だがまあ、決まってしまったものは仕方ない。なんだかんだ言っても新しい経験というのは胸が躍る。
lines.english: Still, what was decided was decided. Whatever I might say, a new experience set my heart racing.

lines.japanese: 俺の中の五分の二は、面白そうなことが無条件に好きだった。
lines.english: Two fifths of me loved anything that sounded entertaining, unconditionally.

lines.japanese: そして五分の一は渡来明日香とのセッションということで浮かれていたし、五分の一はかつて他次元でマンティコアだったころの自分が思いだされて懐かしいと涙ぐんでいた。
lines.english: One fifth was delighted at the prospect of a session with Asuka Watarai, while another fifth was shedding nostalgic tears at the memory of his former life as a manticore in another dimension.

lines.japanese: 「ふう……しかし思ったより道が混んでたせいで遅れ気味だな。ちょっと急いだ方がいいかもしれん」
lines.english: “Hmm... The roads were more crowded than I expected, so we're running a little late. We may want to hurry.”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫。受付終了まであと二十分以上あるから」
lines.english: “We're fine. Check-in doesn't close for more than twenty minutes.”

lines.japanese: 山科京が左手の裾をくいっと上げて、女ものの時計を見せてくれた。
lines.english: Kyou Yamashina tugged up her left sleeve and showed me a woman's wristwatch.

lines.japanese: しかし腕時計よりも、手首を覆っている意味ありげな包帯の方が気になってしまった。な、なぜ彼女はそのような部位に傷を……。
lines.english: But instead of the watch, my attention went to the suggestive bandages covering her wrist. Wh-why did she have an injury in such a place...?

lines.japanese: 「山科さん……まあ、なんだ、死にたいほどの悩みがあったらいつでも俺に相談してくれ。俺たち友達じゃないか」
lines.english: “Yamashina... Well, if you ever have troubles so great you want to die, you can always talk to me. We're friends, aren't we?”

lines.japanese: 俺の中のタカシ的な部分が献身的に申しでた。
lines.english: The Takashi part of me made this devoted offer.

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ、ありがと。話五分の一で聞いておくよ」
lines.english: “Hee-hee. Thanks. I’ll take a fifth of that seriously.”

lines.japanese: うっ、相変わらずカンのいいやつだ。だが──
lines.english: Oof. Sharp as ever. But—

lines.japanese: 「──うむ、それは丁度いい塩梅だ。俺たちは友達だけど、親友ではないからな」
lines.english: “—indeed, that is the perfect proportion. We are friends, but we are not best friends.”

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに俺が親友と呼ぶのは、この世でただひとり森里和馬君だけなんだ。あ、森里君が体育のサッカーでハットトリックを決めたときの武勇伝聞きたい？　聞きたいよね、聞くべきだよ、超カッコいいんだよ」
lines.english: “Incidentally, there is only one man in this world whom I call my best friend: Kazuma Morisato. Oh, want to hear the heroic tale of the time he scored a hat trick in soccer class? You want to. You should. He was unbelievably cool.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そこまでの余裕はないかな」
lines.english: “Mm, I don't think we have that much time.”

lines.japanese: 山科京がふたたび腕時計を上げた。ああ残念、たしかに森里君の魅力を余すところなく伝えるには、軽く二時間以上必要だからな。
lines.english: Kyou Yamashina raised her watch again. What a shame. She was right, though. It would take me at least two hours to communicate the full extent of Morisato's appeal.

lines.japanese: まあ仕方ない、とりあえずいまは社務所の方へ向かうとしよ──
lines.english: It couldn't be helped. For now, we would continue toward the shrine office—

lines.japanese: 「あーっ、先輩アレ！　自分戦隊オレンジャーのお面もあるよ！」
lines.english: “Oh, look, Kuroudo! They have *Self Squadron Me-Ranger* masks too!”

lines.japanese: 「ええい、またおまえか、渡り廊下渡る子。俺とてミラクル・チャイルド・メタモルフォーズして無邪気に走りまわりたいのを自制しているというのに……」
lines.english: “For heaven's sake, you again, Wataruko Watarirouka! I too wish to perform a Miracle Child Metamorphosis and run about innocently, yet I restrain myself...”

lines.japanese: 「おいハリュー・クロード。年長者として、あんたからも一言……」
lines.english: “Hey, Claude Haryuu. As the eldest, tell them—”

lines.japanese: 「明日香、コシフリーヌ女王ないかコシフリーヌ女王」
lines.english: “Asuka, do they have Queen Hip-Shaker? Queen Hip-Shaker.”

lines.japanese: 「こっちもか！」
lines.english: “You too?!”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃガキ向けヒーロー番組つっても、蛎崎が出るんじゃなァ、チェックしないわけいかないでしょう」
lines.english: “Even if it is a children's superhero show, Uni Kakizaki is in it. I can hardly neglect to watch.”

lines.japanese: 「こっ、この男は……不良バンドマンのくせにどんだけ蛎崎うに好きなんだよ」
lines.english: “Th-this man... You're a delinquent rocker. How much can you possibly love Uni Kakizaki?”

lines.japanese: 「趣向を追求するのに、体面を気にする必要はないと思うよ。そういえばＫｕＲｉＹａも初期ロックバードの詞で『ガキのお遊戯、大衆音楽、俺が認めりゃそれはアート』なんて言ってたなぁ」
lines.english: “I see no reason to worry about appearances when pursuing one's tastes. Now that I think of it, KuRiYa wrote in an early Rockbird song, ‘Children's games, popular music—if I approve it, then it is art.’”

lines.japanese: 「あン？　あれ栗山が書いたことになってたか？　ありゃア、俺が立ちションしながら考えたんだけどな」
lines.english: “Huh? Did Kuriyama get credit for that? I came up with it while taking a piss.”

lines.japanese: 「素敵な夢物語だね」
lines.english: “What a lovely fairy tale.”

lines.japanese: 山科京は力なく嘆息した。ちょっとしんどそうだ。まあ、気持ちは分からないでもない。
lines.english: Kyou Yamashina sighed weakly. She looked a little worn out. I could hardly blame her.

lines.japanese: 「じょわっ！　ドーパミン光線！」
lines.english: “Jwah! Dopamine Ray!”

lines.japanese: 学園のプリンセスはいつの間にかお面買ってるし……。
lines.english: At some point, the princess of the academy had bought herself a mask...

lines.japanese: 「ファック！　コルチゾール・フィールド展開！」
lines.english: “Fuck! Cortisol Field, deploy!”

lines.japanese: 柳木原のカリスマアーティストも同レベルで張りあうし……。
lines.english: And Yanagihara's charismatic artist was fighting back on precisely the same level...

lines.japanese: 「まったく、おまえらいい加減にしろ！　アドレナリンスパーク！」
lines.english: “Enough, both of you! Adrenaline Spark!”

lines.japanese: となれば世界の羽田、地上の奇跡とも謳われる俺が参戦しないわけにはいかない。
lines.english: At that point, Haneda of the world—the miracle upon the earth—could hardly decline to join the battle.

lines.japanese: 「ダァー！」
lines.english: “Daaah!”

lines.japanese: 「シィーット！」
lines.english: “Shiiit!”

lines.japanese: 「がるるるーん！」
lines.english: “Garururu!”

lines.japanese: 俺たちが三すくみの牽制を始めると、にわかに辺りの風通しがよくなった。
lines.english: As the three of us began our triangular standoff, the area around us suddenly became much easier to move through.

lines.japanese: ああそうか、通行人の皆さんがキモがって避けていかれるのですね。
lines.english: Oh, I see. All the other pedestrians were creeped out and giving us a wide berth.

lines.japanese: 「ととと、いかんいかん。ぱね田くんがいるとつい行動が同レベルになるよね」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa. We mustn't get carried away. Having Paneda around always brings my behavior down to his level.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　ふざけんなコラ、俺と同レベルってこた神だぞ。神かテメエ、祈るぞ。ブッ拝むぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Huh? Fuck you. Being on my level makes you a god. You a god, asshole? I'll pray to you. I'll fucking worship you.”

lines.japanese: 「てかもー、黙ってないで止めてよ山科ぁ……」
lines.english: “Come on, Yamashina, don't just stand there. Stop us...”

lines.japanese: 「って、あれ？　山科は？」
lines.english: “Wait. Where is Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「げっ……おい大変だ、山科さんはぐれちゃったぞ」
lines.english: “Crap... This is bad. We lost Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「なあ。あそこに転がってる黒い塊なに」
lines.english: “Hey. What's that black lump on the ground over there?”

lines.japanese: 「ああっ、山科京があああー！」
lines.english: “Oh no! Kyou Yamashinaaaa!”

lines.japanese: 彼女は人いきれに当てられ、貧血を起こしていましたとさ。
lines.english: The stifling heat of the crowd had made her faint.

lines.japanese: めでたしめでたし。
lines.english: And they all lived happily ever after.
